newsitem.title: UK: Mexico 500 bln lire five-year FRN due next week.
newsitem.headline: Mexico 500 bln lire five-year FRN due next week.

text.p: Mexico plans to issue a 500 billion lire five-year floating-rate note next week, syndicate managers said on Friday.
The launch was likely on Thursday and Deutsche Morgan Grenfell was tipped as lead manager. The paper was expected to yield in the high 200s basis points over swaps.

This will be the first lira bond launched by Mexico and the first lira FRN issued by an emerging market borrower. Latin American credits have actively tapped the sector this year, opting for fixed-rate bonds.
"Although Mexico is launching an FRN, the investor base for this and fixed-rate bonds is largely the same," said a syndicate manager at a European bank.
"There might be a slightly bigger institutional component among the buyers, but the paper will still be placed mainly in Italy," he said.
Two weeks ago Argentina issued a 500 billion lire seven-year transaction, adding another maturity to its one-, three- and five-year outstanding lira paper.
Pemex, the Mexican state oil company, tapped the sector in March with a 300 billion lire two-year straight bond.
